Thus Porson for βέλτιον [better], which is in Athenaeus 9 p. 375c.
Both forms are poetic for βελτίων [better] and βέλτιστος [best], of which there is one example in Aeschylus, Ag. 379 ὑπὲρ τὸ βέλτιστον [beyond the best].
